title: How a disclosure moves
summary: The public page is the last step. A record appears here only after a private report and a real chance to ship a fix.

content.value: I confirm the flaw on a maintained version, report it privately, and wait for the patch or the agreed window before the CVE is written up here.

items.value: Confirm the flaw on a maintained version, with a clear impact and a suggested correction.
Send the report privately to the project, usually through its GitHub security advisory.
Wait for the patch, or for the agreed disclosure window.
Publish the CVE record here, beside the original notes, the timeline, and the commit that closed it.

content.value: The markdown notes stay in the product folder. The site reads a JSON article with the same sections: summary, weakness, impact, and remediation. Figures are the screenshots already published with the disclosure.

The notes cover application code that trusts the wrong boundary: evaluation of untrusted formulas, sessions that outlive an account, tokens left behind when a user is disabled, and passwords stored with a broken hash.
